pains.label: Can't get owners to list: no listings, lead generation costs money
pains.definition: The broker has no sellable businesses to list. Getting owners to sell means cold outreach, paid leads and ads. Brokers pay for seller leads and lead-generation services.
pains.reasoning: Broker-facing titles ask what to say to get listings and why new brokers fail to get owners to sell; several vendors sell seller leads to brokers.

pains.label: Owners want an unrealistic price; the broker has to set expectations or turn the listing down
pains.definition: The owner's asking price is above what buyers will pay. The broker must talk the owner down, decline the listing, or carry an overpriced listing that will not sell.
pains.reasoning: A broker asks whether to take a seller with unrealistic price expectations; other broker videos are about the seller expectation problem and rejecting a million-dollar price tag.

pains.label: Most listings never sell; months of work on a success fee earns nothing
pains.definition: Seventy to eighty percent of businesses brought to market do not sell. The broker is paid on success, so a listing that sits for months or never sells is unpaid work.
pains.reasoning: Broker blogs and third-party posts repeat that 70 to 80 percent of businesses do not sell and ask how many listings sell once brought to market.

pains.label: Deals under LOI die in due diligence; deal fatigue kills the sale
pains.definition: A signed letter of intent falls apart during due diligence: data requests drag on, buyers find problems, parties retrade or walk. The broker loses the fee after most of the work is done.
pains.reasoning: Broker posts about deal killers, dead deals, deal fatigue and why half of business sales fall apart in due diligence.

pains.label: Buyer's SBA or bank financing falls through; SBA rule changes and lenders' add-back scrutiny move the goalposts
pains.definition: Most small-business deals need an SBA 7(a) loan. Loans get denied, lenders strip add-backs from the broker's SDE, and the SBA changed its rules (SOP 50 10 8, June 2025) on seller notes and eligibility, so deals that worked before now do not close.
pains.reasoning: Records cover SBA loan denials, banks and add-backs, lenders stripping broker add-backs, and the SOP 50 10 8 changes and what they mean for deals.

pains.label: Finding buyers who can actually close: tire kickers, NDAs, proof of funds, buyer lists
pains.definition: Many buyers sign NDAs and never close. The broker must screen for proof of funds, build buyer lists and do outreach to find a buyer who can pay.
pains.reasoning: Titles on how brokers find and choose qualified buyers, buyers who never close, proof of funds, blacklisting NDA signers and building buyer lists.

pains.label: Owners ask if the broker is worth the fee, negotiate it down, or sell without one
pains.definition: Owners question the commission, ask to negotiate a reduced fee, resist retainers, or try to sell without a broker. The broker must justify how they get paid.
pains.reasoning: Records ask whether brokers are worth the money, whether the fee can be negotiated down, and brokers write about retainers versus success fees and how they get paid.

pains.label: Getting cut out of the deal or fighting for an unpaid commission
pains.definition: Buyers and sellers go around the broker after being introduced, or dispute when the commission is due. The broker relies on non-circumvention clauses and sometimes lawyers to get paid.
pains.reasoning: A broker video on preventing sellers and buyers from cutting you out, legal pieces on non-circumvention clauses for brokers, and an owner in a dispute over when the commission is due.

pains.label: The trade's bad reputation: 'used car salesmen', 'scam', 'unprofessional brokers'
pains.definition: Buyers and owners distrust business brokers as a class. Brokers write about the industry's terrible reputation and have to overcome it to win listings and buyers.
pains.reasoning: A brokerage blog on why the industry has a terrible reputation, videos asking if brokers are a scam, buyer complaints of unprofessional behavior and dishonest brokers.

pains.label: New and franchise brokers work commission-only for months with no closed deal; training and management let them down
pains.definition: Most new brokers fail. They work commission-only, wait a long time for a first deal, and reviews of the big franchises complain about training, pay and management.
pains.reasoning: Titles say 91 percent of new brokers fail, ask how to land a first deal, and franchise employee reviews complain about management and pay.

pains.label: Pricing the business and defending the number: SDE add-backs, multiples, comps and the CIM
pains.definition: The broker must produce a valuation and a confidential information memorandum (CIM, the sales document), then justify the multiple and add-backs to buyers and lenders who challenge them.
pains.reasoning: A broker asks how to establish the proper SDE multiple and justify the valuation; others ask how brokers make CIMs; vendors sell comps and automated valuations to brokers.

pains.label: Broker tools cost too much or the data is doubtful: CRMs, comps databases, data rooms, listing sites
pains.definition: Brokers pay for CRMs, comparable-sales databases, virtual data rooms and marketplace listings. They question the price (why pay $50K+?), hidden fees, and whether the comps data is verified.
pains.reasoning: Questions on whether PeerComps and DealStats data is good and verified, vendor posts on hidden costs of generic CRMs and data room pricing, a complaint video about BizBuySell.

pains.label: State licence and SEC rules: what a business broker may do without a real estate or securities licence
pains.definition: Some states (California, Florida) require a real estate licence to broker businesses, and the SEC M&A broker exemption sets limits. Brokers must know the rules to avoid unlicensed activity.
pains.reasoning: Official pages on business-opportunity brokerage licensing, an association page on unlicensed activity, the SEC M&A brokers letter, and questions on becoming a licensed broker.
